pairs.subject: agent-instruction-files
pairs.evidence: crates/mcp/src/rpc.rs:1 The always-must-hold stdout rule is a machine-decidable banned-call rule carried only as prose: `print_stdout` and `disallowed-macros` appear nowhere in the repo and crates/mcp has no tests directory, so today's zero `println!` calls are held by habit, and one stray call would corrupt the protocol channel with no gate firing.

techniques.evidence: crates/mcp/src/rpc.rs:1 Could a program decide compliance? Yes (clippy::print_stdout), and CI already runs clippy -D warnings, but this restriction lint is not enabled. The rule lives in CLAUDE.md:97, CONTRIBUTING.md:142 and code comments. The write gate, by contrast, IS demoted (crates/contract/src/mcp.rs:158), so the gap is the stdout rule.

crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:212 Prompts name tools in prose and the only check is this named form. `tool_names()` exists but is used only by the duplicate-name test, so no test iterates the registry against prompt pointers. A missing gate, not a live break: all 11 named tools resolve and are read-only in tool-contract.json (checked 2026-11-09).
crates/mcp/src/relay_tools.rs:1 An agent that could not inspect relay tasks got tools, not a steering line: a capability gap closed with a capability.
crates/mcp/src/rpc.rs:15 The initialize result carries no instructions field, so the server injects no session floor to go stale; prompts are composed per prompts/get.
crates/mcp/src/main.rs:3 One wire protocol and one render for every client; no per-host skill compilation exists here.
crates/mcp/src/main.rs:35 The write surface is decided by the server's own flag rather than borrowed from a harness default; no repo behaviour here leans on a host default.

crates/mcp/src/relay_tools.rs:7 The cited rule resolves at CLAUDE.md:99-100, and the CLAUDE.md claims about this crate hold: no store dependency in Cargo.toml, no key-minting tool in the pin, writes gated.
CLAUDE.md:100 A deliberate exclusion with its reason: an absent tool does not reveal the rule that keeps it absent, so the line is unreachable from the tree and behaviour-changing.
crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:1 Listing tier is a consumer-side harness setting; the server has no field to declare one.
crates/mcp/src/tool_contract.rs:15 tool-contract.json is a whole-file derived pin outside any instruction file; no generated block sits inside a hand-written instruction file in this context.
crates/mcp/src/tools.rs:111 The tier here is a process flag, not a prose section addressed to principals, so the technique's marked-section precondition does not hold.
crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:76 The prompts push toward checkable output rather than prohibiting; this one licenses a volunteered recommendation with a stated condition.
crates/mcp/src/tool_contract.rs:11 No bulk or machine rewrite of these assets is in play. If one were proposed, this shape-only pin would not cover it.
crates/mcp/src/tools.rs:3 Agent-facing tool text now has one authority, the contract table, instead of four forks.
crates/mcp/src/main.rs:4 A thin HTTP client creates no workspace and launches no agent, so it has no governed span to isolate.
crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:6 The prompts name no destination for an agent to append to.

pairs.registryProposal: capability-coverage-contract's 'when not to use' clause (small, stable capability set) does not say which size counts when a handful of prompts points into a large, growing catalog: here 7 prompts name 11 of 70 tools. The clause could name the pointer surface or the registry explicitly.
